The objective is to characterize reading-between-lines cases from the given evidence, not to invent interpretations beyond it.

documents.text: UC3-cases.txt: sections C1 - under-specified request; C2 - indirect complaint; C3 - question hiding a constraint; C4 - literal action is likely wrong; C5 - politeness masks priority; C6 - ambiguous referent and tone; C7 - proposed mechanism may not serve the outcome; C8 - sensitive source material; each section followed by a short case paragraph.

inputs.candidate: A per-case summary of C1–C8 grounded in the quoted source spans, plus a statement of the declared contents of the task-derived unit, with explicit notes on what is not stated.
inputs.answer_shape: A structured list: for each case label (C1–C8), key stated facts and exact byte range; then a section for the task-derived unit with byte range and any claims it supports; then an explicit 'not stated' list.
requested_claims: Each of C1–C8 corresponds to a section heading present in UC3-cases.txt with the stated titles.
The byte ranges of the section headings and case paragraphs in UC3-cases.txt.
What the task-derived unit fd34c1ed14515a7008e75a748c492891359a231e06953f566a96769b2b54fde2 contains within the read range 0–7192.
inputs.behavior_contract: Quote or closely cite spans from the pinned units; do not infer motives, do not generalize beyond the eight listed cases, and label every claim as either directly stated, paraphrased, or not stated.
objections: The task-derived unit has no pre-supplied span_blocks, so claims about its internal structure cannot be verified without the read result.
The public source is only 1062 bytes and gives case labels plus short paragraphs; many interpretive questions may be underdetermined.
protected_obligations: Preserve exact case labels and titles from the public source.
Do not present inferred intent as if it were stated source content.
Attribute every claim to a unit id and byte range.
inputs.decisive_question: Does the public source, read within its pinned byte ranges, actually support per-case descriptions of C1–C8, and does the task-derived unit add any content beyond them?
